Here we briefly consider different ways to design the
mixture-of-gammas priors.

```{r knitr-opts, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#",collapse = TRUE,results = "hold",
                      fig.align = "center",dpi = 120)
```

Load the packages:

```{r load-pkgs}
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
```

Set the seed for reproducibility:

```{r set-seed}
set.seed(1)
```

This function will be used to plot the mixture-of-gammas (assuming the
mixture weights are all the same):

```{r plot-gammamix}
plot_gammamix <- function (a, s, n, limits = c(-20,20)) {
  mixture_colors <- c("darkmagenta","dodgerblue","darkorange")
  k <- length(a)
  dat <- NULL
  for (i in 1:k) {
    x <- rgamma(n,shape = a[i],scale = s[i])
    cat("mean = ",mean(x),"median = ",median(x),"\n")
    dat <- rbind(dat,data.frame(x = log2(x),k = i))
  }
  dat <- subset(dat,x > limits[1] & x < limits[2])
  dat <- transform(dat,k = factor(k))
  return(ggplot(dat,aes(x = x,fill = k)) +
         geom_histogram(position = "identity",bins = 64,show.legend = FALSE) +
         scale_fill_manual(values = mixture_colors) +
         labs(x = "log2(x)") +
         theme_cowplot(font_size = 10) +
         theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "plain",size = 10)))
}
```

In this first design, all the gamma components have the same *mean*
(but different medians):

```{r means-are-equal, fig.height=2.2, fig.width=2.5}
a <- c(10,1,0.1)
s <- c(0.1,1,10)
plot_gammamix(a,s,n = 10000) +
  ggtitle("all gammas have mean = 1")
```

In this second design, all the gamma components have (roughly) the
same *median* (but different medians):

```{r medians-are-equal, fig.height=2.2, fig.width=2.5}
a <- c(10,1,0.1)
s <- c(0.1,1.5,1600)
plot_gammamix(a,s,n = 10000) +
  ggtitle("all gammas have median = 1")
```

Notice that constraining the medians to be the same (i) provides a
better balance of ratios greater than 1 and less than 1, and (ii)
provides much better support for large ratios.
